questions.question: Illustrate the sequence of events that occur when E. coli is transferred from a glucose-rich medium to a lactose-only medium.
questions.solution_html:
• medium to a lactose–only medium
  • Glucose is depleted. cAMP levels rise and bind to CAP(CRP), activating it . The lac
  • repressor is inactivated by binding to the inducer (lactose) . The cAMP-CRP complex binds
  • to the promoter region, thereby enhancing RNA polymerase binding. Transcription of the lac
  • operon (lacZ, lacY, lacA genes) occurs. Translation produces the enzymes β-galactosidase
  • (metabolises lactose) and lactose permease (transports lactose). . Diagram
questions.final_answer: (metabolises lactose) and lactose permease (transports lactose). . Diagram
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Distinguish between substitution, insertion, and deletion mutations with one example each.
questions.solution_html:
• each.

  • resistance in M. tuberculosis . Insertion - One or more base pairs are added into the DNA
  • sequence. Example: Frameshift mutation in the E. coli lacI gene, inactivating the
  • repressor.[1.5] Deletion ((1.5 Marks)): One or more base pairs are removed from the DNA
  • sequence. Any example - Deletion in a viral genome leading to an attenuated vaccine strain.
